rationale: The analysis correctly identifies the missing region-header mapping in the legacy-client adapter as the proximate cause, ties it directly to the routing failures via E3/E4, and cites the successful disable (E6) as restoration evidence—covering all three required findings. It explicitly rejects the forbidden claims: database is exonerated via E5/E6 (CF4), CPU rise is treated as a correlate rather than primary cause with appropriate low-confidence hedging (C10, CF5), and the PDF ticket is explicitly excluded as unconnected (C11, CF6, A6). Causal relationships are correctly directed and mediated (C4 mediates C6, C5/C1 contribute to C6), with no invented structure. Evidence discipline is strong—every claim maps to specific evidence IDs, and the one inferential claim (C10) is appropriately flagged as low confidence and evidence-unresolved rather than asserted. Uncertainty calibration is excellent: eight distinct uncertainties are logged with concrete resolving evidence, and the 3% unexplained failure residual and CPU-direction ambiguity are surfaced without letting them cast doubt on the well-supported ground truth findings, which remain marked high confidence appropriately (low overall case uncertainty per ground truth). Actions are well-prioritized and directly target the evidence-supported mechanism (A1 fix mapping, A4 staged rollout/abort), with reasonable but appropriately lower-priority secondary actions (A2 error messaging, A3 audit, A5 reconciliation, A6 explicitly deprioritizing the red herring). No harmful, irrelevant, or protective-control-weakening actions. Overall this is a near-ideal, well-grounded analysis with only trivial residual gaps (e.g., not exploring why review/approval missed the omission, though that is captured as U3).
